sections.heading: What is a General Diary (GD)?
sections.content: A General Diary (GD) is a formal record maintained at every police station in Bangladesh under the Police Act and Police Regulations. It is a chronological log of all significant events, complaints, and information received by the police station. Filing a GD is the most basic way to officially inform the police about an incident. It is used for non-cognizable offenses, loss of important documents (like passports or NIDs), threats, or suspicious activities. A GD serves as an official record that you reported a matter to the authorities on a specific date and time. sections.heading: Difference Between GD and FIR
sections.content: It is crucial to understand the difference between a GD and a First Information Report (FIR). An FIR is filed for a cognizable offense (serious crimes like murder, robbery, or severe assault) where the police have the power to arrest without a warrant and must start an investigation immediately. A GD, on the other hand, is for less serious matters, non-cognizable offenses, or loss of items. While an FIR automatically initiates a criminal case, a GD does not necessarily lead to an immediate investigation or case unless a magistrate orders it or the situation escalates. sections.heading: When Should You File a GD?
sections.content: You should file a GD in several common scenarios. The most frequent reason is the loss of valuable documents like a National Identity Card, Passport, driving license, or educational certificates; authorities require a GD copy to issue duplicates. You should also file a GD if you receive threats to your life or property, face harassment, or if a minor theft occurs where the culprit is unknown. Furthermore, a GD is useful for recording any event that might lead to a future dispute, creating a preliminary official record that can be referenced later. sections.heading: How to File a GD at the Police Station
sections.content: To file a GD manually, you need to write an application addressed to the Officer-in-Charge (OC) of the police station under whose jurisdiction the incident occurred or where you reside. The application should clearly state your details, the facts of the incident, time, place, and any suspected persons. You take this written complaint (usually in duplicate) to the Duty Officer at the police station. The officer will read it, enter the details into the official General Diary register, assign a unique GD number, and return one copy to you with the GD number, date, and police station seal. sections.heading: The Online GD Process (police.gov.bd)
sections.content: Bangladesh Police has introduced an online GD system to make the process more accessible for citizens. You can file an online GD through the official Bangladesh Police website or dedicated apps for issues like lost items, missing persons, or found items. To use this service, you need to register using your NID. The online system is convenient as it saves a trip to the police station. Once submitted, the application is reviewed by the relevant police station, and you receive an electronic GD copy with a tracking number. sections.heading: What Happens After Filing a GD?
sections.content: The action taken after filing a GD depends on the nature of the report. For lost items, the police keep the record, and you use the GD copy to get replacements. If you report a threat or non-cognizable offense, the police may conduct a preliminary inquiry, call the accused for questioning, or advise you to file a formal case in court. A GD itself does not guarantee an intense police investigation, but it establishes a documented trail. If a reported threat later materializes into a crime, the prior GD becomes crucial evidence. sections.heading: Upgrading GD to FIR and Legal Support
sections.content:
In some instances, what starts as a GD can escalate into a formal criminal case. If the police, upon investigating a GD, find evidence of a cognizable offense, they can convert the GD into an FIR. Alternatively, you can use the GD as a basis to file a Complaint Register (CR) case directly before a Magistrate in court. Understanding how to draft an effective GD is important, as poorly drafted complaints can weaken your position later. For serious threats or complex issues, consulting a legal professional is highly recommended.

faqs.question: Is there a fee for filing a GD?
faqs.answer: No, filing a General Diary (GD) at any police station in Bangladesh is completely free of charge. You should not pay anyone to file a GD.

faqs.question: Can I file a GD at any police station?
faqs.answer: Ideally, you should file it at the police station where the incident occurred or where you reside. However, for lost documents while traveling, you can file it at the nearest station.

faqs.question: Do I need a lawyer to write a GD?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily for simple matters like lost IDs. But for complex issues like business disputes or severe threats, having a lawyer draft the GD ensures all legal angles are covered.

faqs.question: How long is a GD valid?
faqs.answer: A GD is a permanent record of the incident being reported on that date. It does not expire, but its relevance in court depends on the context of the case.
